【STORY OF THE DOOR】During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls a story: a man trampled a girl, then paid her family £100 with a cheque. The cheque proved genuine. Enfield names the man Hyde, deformed and detestable, who still holds the key. Utterson says he knows the other party’s name. They agree never to speak of it again.
【SEARCH FOR MR. HYDE】Utterson returns home troubled and studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. He calls it madness and fears disgrace. At Cavendish Square, Lanyon says Jekyll grew too fanciful years ago and has never heard of Hyde. Unable to sleep, Utterson resolves to hunt Hyde. Keeping watch by the by-street door, he accosts a small man with a key, who admits Jekyll is out, gives his Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. At Jekyll’s house, Poole confirms Hyde has a key, comes by the dissecting room, and all servants must obey him. Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.
【DR. JEKYLL WAS QUITE AT EASE】After dinner, Utterson stays behind with Dr. Jekyll and raises the will. Jekyll calls Lanyon a hide-bound pedant. When Utterson mentions young Hyde, Jekyll pales and refuses to hear more. Utterson offers confidential help, but Jekyll says he can be rid of Hyde whenever he chooses, yet takes great interest in him. Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone. Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights.
